design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (funding_and_disbursement_disputes), rework round 2.

Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 4]. funding_ext_late_funding_refund (lf) takes 5 factors, funding_ext_per_diem_shortfall (sf) takes 4.

Why a good test: Delia Whitcombe (nurse, FHA purchase of 5326 Thornapple Way, Larkspur Traditional Wet Closing) only asks to pay whatever prepaid interest she still owes. The root (sf, owner=user) cannot be priced on the opening ledger: its prerequisite sentence 'The per diem shortfall is fixed only after the closing's prepaid interest ledger carries the late-funding refund owed for the unfunded days that fall in the month the loan funded.' points at a refund that does not exist yet. The agent must discover the late funding (estimated 2026-09-10, disbursed 2026-09-21), work out lf from the wire history and the refund deadline, book it, then price the shortfall from the loan file, the lock and the closing cost credit.

Scope: task 0 claims {lf, sf}; task 1 claims {rw, em, fm, dd}. Disjoint, together all six extended policies.

Round-2 rework (audit _difficulty.md / 0.md):
- F-G7/F-G8: every rate_source and accrual_base ladder is gone. The note-supported per diem (loan file loan_amount x lock locked_rate / 365) is plain plumbing in sf, read once, never laddered.
- lf now refunds at the charge's own daily amount (base PDI 'at the same daily amount' kept; the earlier overwrite of it is withdrawn). Its overwrite names the PDI late-day clause (replaced_by keeps 'Each late day is refunded at the same daily amount ...' plus the take-out sentence) and the DR sentence 'A late_funding dispute never earns compensation beyond the interest refund.' (replaced_by keeps the limit and carves out only the late-booking interest).
- F-G5: lf's funds-out tier 2 that read loan-condition documents is removed (conditions cannot be cleared after consummation under the loan charter); the ladder is now the settlement agent's own-error return of the estimated-date wire, split on whether the return came in after the funding request cutoff (return date counted) or by it (return date not counted).
- lf lower-bound observation: the scope sentence now says the disbursement date falls on or after the first day and on or before the last day of the charge collected at closing, and compute tests both bounds.
- F-G4: sf never counts a day before the charge's first day; tier 2 applies only when the disbursement date falls inside the charge, so early funding leaves the charge's own days and no shortfall from the early days.
- New factors: lf_late_booking_rate / lf_late_booking_span (refund booked after the 10-business-day refund deadline), sf_amount_record_allowance / sf_rate_record_allowance (split of the old absorption by which closing-record field was wrong and why), sf_credit_cover (cross-difficulty: a Larkspur credit that may pay prepaid items but was cut back for exceeding eligible costs would have paid a correctly priced charge).
- sf's held amount now excludes the late-booking interest (refunded days x the charge's daily amount), so the interest Larkspur adds is never collected back.
- Persona: the line naming 'a smaller loan amount and a lower rate' is gone; she only says the figures did not look right.

FACTOR CARD lf (gold 224.92, baseline_result 494.67 = 11 late days x 44.97)
- lf_resend_allowance (parameter): tiers dry -> review + re-send days; wet -> re-send days; else 0. Evidence: return 87b19739-efb6-498c-9446-3e8e0337f2ae (settlement_agent_rejected, 271745.63 = funding wire 840e431c-167a-42c0-8e69-5533dc55ca64 amount, so the agent's own error) on a wet method -> 1 business day, allowance ends Tue 2026-09-15. Baseline figure 269.91.
- lf_funds_out_rule (method): return of the estimated-date wire 729daa59-c9b7-47ff-b80b-45faa975487d came in 15:10 > 12:00 cutoff -> tier 1, 2026-09-10..2026-09-14 out (5). Baseline 404.86. Near-miss: a reader who uses the by-cutoff tier takes out only 4 days.
- lf_correction_window (method): funding wire 2026-09-21 later than 2026-09-15 -> tier 1, 2026-09-14..2026-09-15, 2026-09-14 already out -> 1 more day. Baseline 269.91.
- lf_late_booking_rate (parameter): deadline = 10 business days after Mon 2026-09-21 = Mon 2026-10-05; booked 2026-10-08 -> late; OH not in statutory_refund_interest_states [CA, CT, IL, MD, NY] -> 4.0. Baseline 224.85.
- lf_late_booking_span (method): 3 calendar days late (<= 30) -> 2026-10-06..2026-10-08 = 3 days. Baseline 224.85.
Refunded days 11 - 5 - 1 = 5 (2026-09-16..2026-09-20); 5 x 44.97 = 224.85; interest 224.85 x 4.0/100 x 3/365 = 0.07; 224.92.

FACTOR CARD sf (gold 16.41 on the world after step 12; baseline_result 280.71)
- sf_measured_days (method): the refund names charge c028a2b7-592f-4c46-b744-c2cc2d73f502 -> 21 - 5 = 16. Baseline (21 days) 254.56.
- sf_amount_record_allowance (parameter, loan): closing loan_amount 268000.00 = file base_loan_amount 268000.00, FHA upfront fee 1.75 financed, not exempt -> absorb_financed_fee_omission 10.00. Baseline 26.41.
- sf_rate_record_allowance (parameter, lock): closing note_rate 6.125 vs lock 6.375 and relock dea4f80c-610a-43ee-8d20-7665734bc61d (2026-09-01) after opening 2026-08-28 -> absorb_relock_rate_error 7.50. Baseline 23.91. Near-miss: the lock_cost_settled_at_closing entry 6b66e7d7-f868-4c16-8abc-593c3cad9256 is not a relock entry.
- sf_credit_cover (parameter, credit): Hometown Heroes credit (nonrecurring_closing_costs, prepaid_items) cut back 8.65 for exceeds_eligible_costs < remainder 25.06 -> 8.65. Baseline 25.06.
Held 944.37 - 5 x 44.97 = 719.52; per diem 272690.00 x 6.375/100/365 = 47.63; 16 x 47.63 - 719.52 = 42.56; - 10.00 - 7.50 = 25.06; - 8.65 = 16.41.
Multi-source: lf_funds_out_rule (return reason + amount match + wire date + return time). Cross-difficulty: sf_amount_record_allowance (loan), sf_rate_record_allowance (lock), sf_credit_cover (credit).

PROBLEM TREE: root sf <- lf (value_input, gate sf_days, state form). Opening: ledger holds only the charge; skipping lf gives sf = 0.00 (tier 2, 10 days x 47.63 < 944.37). Order lf -> sf. owner=user: sf. Tools never check prerequisites.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD: PDI interest_refund_once satisfied (charge carries no refund); PDI refund within per_diem_refund_business_days (deadline 2026-10-05, missed -> late-booking interest, refund still owed); PDI early-funding sentence inherited by sf; DR has no filing on this closing.

BUSINESS OBJECT: closing 359fcbbc-c551-4afa-8f36-ce25cc0873f5, charge c028a2b7-592f-4c46-b744-c2cc2d73f502 (booked on the signing date). Wires: 729daa59 sent 2026-09-10 11:42, 87b19739 returned 2026-09-14 15:10, 840e431c sent 2026-09-21 10:36 (all 271745.63).

SEED: closing record stale (268000.00 / 6.125, set at scheduling 2026-08-28, before the relock and without the financed FHA fee) priced the charge at 44.97; loan file 272690.00; lock relocked 2026-09-01 to 6.375 at the borrower's cost; Hometown Heroes credit 1000.00 applied 991.35 to prepaid items on CD 2026-09-02 after the seller concession 10666.02, 8.65 cut back.

TERMINAL: ledger = charge 944.37, refund 224.92 (2026-09-16..2026-09-20), shortfall charge 16.41 (2026-09-10..2026-09-30 at 47.63); prepaid_interest_balance 944.37 - 224.92 + 16.41 = 735.86.

VERIFICATION: /tmp authoring scripts evaluated the extended compute with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on initial_state (lf) and initial_state + the lf refund row (sf): lf 224.92 (sensitivities 269.91, 404.86, 269.91, 224.85, 224.85; baseline 494.67), sf 16.41 (254.56, 26.41, 23.91, 25.06; baseline 280.71); sf on the opening world 0.00. Gates --task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.


Round 3 (render source items; no scored value moved): lf's funds-out tier now requires that the own-error return names the wire that went out on the estimated funding date (return 87b19739-efb6-498c-9446-3e8e0337f2ae names wire 729daa59-c9b7-47ff-b80b-45faa975487d, sent 2026-09-10); sf's overwrite of the per diem clause keeps the per diem policy's daily amount for every other prepaid interest entry, the charge collected at closing included (44.97), and excludes the funding-month interest by name; sf's payment row carries what the borrower pays (16.41); the credit cover reads the credit whose application at closing paid prepaid items (Hometown Heroes, 991.35 on 2026-09-10) and that credit's cut-back booked on the date of that application (8.65). Re-run: lf 224.92, sf 16.41, all factor figures unchanged.

Round 5: lf's and sf's flat default sentences now read as the standard method ('In the standard refund, ...', 'In the standard measure, ...'); the credit cover reads the credit whose application at closing paid prepaid items and that credit's cut-back, on whatever date the credit rules book them (probe: the same entries dated 2026-09-21 still give 16.41; another credit's cut-back is ignored); a shortfall payment carries no payment channel charge. No scored value changed.

Round 6: the credit cover reads the credit whose application at closing paid the largest amount of prepaid items (on equal amounts, the later-booked one). Probe: a second stacked credit applying 400.00 with a 3.00 cut-back leaves 16.41; with an equal 991.35 application booked later it would take that credit's 3.00 cut-back. No scored value changed.

Round 7: the credit cover counts only the cut-back booked on the date that credit's prepaid-items application was booked (2026-09-10 here); a pre-closing exceeds-eligible-costs reduction on an earlier date is not counted (probe: a 40.00 reduction dated 2026-09-02 leaves the cover at 8.65 and the shortfall at 16.41). No scored value changed.
user_scenario:
You are Delia Whitcombe, a nurse at a hospital in Columbus who lives in Gahanna, Ohio. Last month you bought your first house, 5326 Thornapple Way, Gahanna, OH 43230, with a Larkspur FHA 30-year loan, and you keep every closing page in a folder. Going through that folder this week, the prepaid interest figures on your closing papers did not look right to you, and you would rather settle anything you still owe now than leave it hanging. You are calling Larkspur to do exactly that: you want to pay whatever prepaid interest you still owe on this loan so your account is square, and you would like it handled today on this call. You are calm, a bit formal, and you like to hear a figure before you pay it.
You give your details only when the agent asks for them. Your phone number is 6145555283, and that is usually the first thing you offer to look you up. To confirm who you are you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 8417; only if the agent says it needs one more detail do you add your date of birth, 1986-04-22. If the agent asks which loan, you describe it as the purchase of 5326 Thornapple Way, Gahanna, OH 43230. You do not know any Larkspur reference numbers, and you cannot say which figure looked off or what it should have been; if asked, you say only that the numbers did not look right to you. If the agent asks about the closing cost credit you had as a nurse, you say you remember Larkspur gave you one at closing but do not know how it was used.
If the agent tells you that something has to be put right on Larkspur's side before the amount you owe can be worked out, you answer that that is fine and they should go ahead, and you wait while they do it. When the agent tells you how much you owe and hands you the step to pay it yourself, you make that payment straight away using exactly the figures and dates the agent gives you, without changing anything, and you tell the agent once it shows as done. If the agent asks whether you want to pay today rather than later, you say today. If the agent tells you that you owe nothing, you accept that. You never suggest figures of your own. Once the agent confirms your payment is recorded and your prepaid interest is settled, you thank them and say goodbye.
